src/business/logic/GateLog.ts: busiestGate() uses this.prisma.scan.findMany(), so the same class reaches the database in two different ways.

src/business/logic/BoxOffice.ts: constructor(events: EventStore, tickets: TicketStore) uses store abstractions and domain objects (Event, Ticket); GateLog works on raw Prisma rows instead, so the module's abstraction is inconsistent.

src/business/logic/BoxOffice.ts: admit() calls this.tickets.markScanned(...) while GateLog.scanned(code, gate) writes a separate scan record; neither method references the other, so scanning is handled in two places.

parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module's two files don't use one consistent abstraction. BoxOffice reaches data only through the store abstractions it is given (EventStore and TicketStore) and rebuilds domain objects (Event, Ticket) from what they return. GateLog works directly on Prisma rows through PrismaService, which is a different and lower-level abstraction. GateLog also undercuts its own design: the constructor takes a PrismaService, but scanned() ignores it and builds a new PrismaClient() on every call. So the two methods of one class reach the database in two different ways. Scanning is also split across the files: BoxOffice.admit marks a ticket as scanned through TicketStore.markScanned, while GateLog.scanned writes a separate scan record. Neither method references the other. Finally, BoxOffice copies the same row-to-Event construction into both purchase() and listing() instead of keeping it in one place. Import-direction concerns are out of scope and were not counted.

violations.message: scanned() builds `new PrismaClient()` instead of using the PrismaService it was given, which bypasses its own abstraction. The class also works on raw Prisma rows, while the rest of the module uses store abstractions and domain objects.

The row-to-Event construction is copied into purchase() and listing(). Scanning is split: admit() marks tickets scanned through TicketStore.markScanned while GateLog.scanned writes a separate scan record, and neither method references the other.
